messages.subject: Coding Year and Observer, and Working Through Starting Values
parts:
Hi Chrissy,

It sounds like you might have a sparse data problem. Can you post a summary of the umf?

The AIC problem indicates that the MLEs for some coefficients are probably getting stuck in bad places, again because the information in the data isn't strong enough to find the optimum. Unfortunately, there isn't a great solution for modeling observer effects in this situation without resorting to a random effects structure in BUGS. The 23 fixed effect coefficients for observer will be tough to estimate here without rich data.

I suppose one solution if you knew the data really well would be to label the "good" and "not as good" observers and model that single effect. It would be a rough approximation, but I doubt there are truly 23 differences in observer ability (at least, not that the data could discriminate). The trick is that you can't use the data to determine observer quality - you'd need some a priori info to make it appropriate.
